name: Go
title: Go (1.26)

presenceList.meta: R2, Ec2, Ec8, V7, D3, Q4

preamble.text: Analysis against Go 1.26 (February 2026). Generics have been stable since 1.18 (March 2022) — over 4 years of production use. Go 1.24 added generic type aliases; Go 1.26 adds further generic and runtime improvements.

type.text: **Implicit interfaces radical decoupling**: No declaration of implementation, duck typing at compile time
**Composition over inheritance**: No inheritance, only struct embedding
**Small interfaces**: Convention is single-method interfaces (io.Reader, io.Writer)
**Generics (stable since 1.18)**: Type parameters eliminate `interface{}` casts — `slices.Sort`, `maps.Clone`, `cmp.Or` are type-safe (note: `sync.Map` remains a non-generic `any`-keyed type)
**Range-over-func (1.23)**: Custom iteration patterns via `iter.Seq[T]` decouple iteration protocol from data structure
**No higher-kinded types**: Generics are first-order type parameters only
**`min`/`max`/`clear` builtins (1.21)**: Built-in operations eliminate unnecessary function coupling
**Nil everywhere, and no sum types**: `nil` pointers and nil interfaces couple code to nil checks, and the language has no sum type to replace them
**Interfaces can be nil with non-nil value**: (nil, *T) couples interface semantics

construction.text: **Zero values make sense**: Default initialization doesn't couple to constructors
**Constructors are conventions**: `NewX()` functions, not special syntax
**Can couple to package-level state**: `init()` functions run at import
**Global package state**: Package-level variables couple to initialization order
**Collection order is unpinned**: the specification states map iteration receives no order guarantee, and the runtime randomizes the seed deliberately
**One value, many names**: slices and maps share backing structures — append to a slice can write a buffer another name reads, and the parameter type names a value, not the sharing
**Every transfer names a call**: deferred calls are written at the site (the defer statement is the call), and the interfaces dispatch by method value, not by string

memory.text: **Garbage collection decouples memory**: Concurrent mark-sweep GC with sub-millisecond pause targets
**No manual memory management**: Can't have use-after-free
**Escape analysis optimizes**: Stack allocation when possible, decouples from explicit allocation
**Profile-guided optimization (1.22+)**: Compiler uses runtime profiles to optimize, decoupling performance from manual tuning
**Defer couples cleanup to function exit**: Not immediate, but predictable
**Simple memory model**: No complex ownership rules
**The class is declared and recoverable**: panics are values in the frame, recover reaches them (documented), and the fatal classes (the runtime's) sit outside the language's surface

error.text: **Explicit error returns**: `func foo() (Result, error)` makes errors visible
**No error composition**: Can't map/flatMap errors natively, so call sites repeat `if err != nil`; generics enable `Result` types but not idiomatically
**Panic exists but rare**: Explicit, but not in type system
**`errors.Join` (1.20)**: Can combine multiple errors, improving composition slightly
**A fault ends the program**: an unrecovered panic terminates the program (documented), and the panicking path unwinds the goroutine it ran on

concurrency.text: **Goroutines separate concurrency**: Lightweight, easy to spawn
**Select decouples multiplexing**: Wait on multiple channels independently
**Structured logging (slog, 1.21)**: Decouples logging concerns from application logic
**Can share memory**: Mutexes allow traditional coupling, but discouraged

platform.text: **Open-source toolchain**: The Go compiler and standard library are BSD-3 licensed and developed in the open
**Alternative implementations**: Gccgo (GCC front end) and TinyGo (microcontrollers, WebAssembly) implement Go independently of the main toolchain
**Portable binaries**: A Go program builds to a static native binary with no installed runtime or virtual machine
**Broad cross-compilation**: One toolchain emits Linux, macOS, Windows, and WebAssembly binaries by setting `GOOS` and `GOARCH`

ecosystem.text: **Standard tooling**: Go build, go test, go fmt
**Project-local conventions**: Build tags, code generation, and layout conventions grew outside the toolchain, so each project's tooling is partly its own
**Cross-compilation**: Easy to build for different platforms
**The plugin path is unpromised**: plugin.Open requires the application and its plugins to be built with the same toolchain version and flags [@goPluginDoc]
**Stored data crosses on a published design**: a gob stream is self-describing, fields match by name and compatible type, and out-of-date receivers keep working as a type gains fields [@goGobs]

evolution.text: **No breaking changes**: Code from 2012 still compiles
**Build variants multiply**: //go:build constraints select which files enter the build, so a package is a platform and tag outcome, not only a directory

domain.text: **Great for CLI tools**: Fast startup, single binary

learning.text: **Quick to productivity**: Can be productive in days
**Few concepts**: Generics are additive; core language remains small and learnable

security.text: The specification defines integer arithmetic as wraparound (module 2^size)

reproducibility.text: **The contract the toolchain reads**: go.mod is read by the go command, and the require directives name versions the build validates

governance.text: **The parser ships as a library**: go/parser is in the standard library, the specification's grammar is normative, and analysis tools run the vendor's parser

supplychain.text: The checksum database signs the module graph, and go.sum records it.
Module paths are namespaced by repository, so names cannot collide.
The project publishes security advisories with CVE mappings.

observability.text: runtime/trace and net/http/pprof ship in the standard library.
log/slog ships structured logging in the standard library.
Panics print full goroutine stack traces by default.

feedback.text: No debugger ships with the toolchain; delve is a separate project.

interop.text: cgo is the in-process foreign interface to C.
Cross-compilation to the common GOOS/GOARCH pairs needs no toolchain changes.

tradeoffs: **The language is deliberately small**: Exceptions, operator overloading, and pattern matching are left out, so programs are longer and each construct is plain — a scope decision
**One formatter settles style**: `gofmt` writes a single canonical layout, trading some expression for a uniform codebase — a tooling convention
**Tooling ships in the `go` command**: Formatting, testing, vetting, and documentation come as one package, so the choice of tools is made by the toolchain rather than by the team
**The Go 1 promise freezes the standard library**: The compatibility guarantee keeps old code building and makes early API decisions permanent — a stability trade

**The standard library is the framework**: `net/http` and `encoding/json` are used directly rather than through a third-party layer, a design choice whose cost is the conveniences such a layer would add
verdict: Go's implicit interfaces provide exceptionally low coupling by decoupling implementation from declaration without explicit `implements` clauses. Goroutines and channels separate concurrency from shared-memory synchronization. Generics, stable for over three years, eliminate `interface{}` casts. Range-over-func enables custom iteration without coupling to built-in loop constructs. Main strength: simplicity prevents complex coupling from emerging. Main weakness: nil is still everywhere, error handling does not compose, and the language has no sum types or pattern matching.

energy.text: Compiles to native code: the fastest class in the language energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy; @pereira2021ranking]. A causal re-analysis attributes the difference to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: A large training corpus and strong code-generation results: models write this language well [@joel2025lowresource; @effibenchx2025].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: A module ships source, and the toolchain compiles every dependency
plugin.Open requires the application and the plugin to be built with the same toolchain version and flags

data_formats.note: Go publishes the promise for stored gobs: a stream is self-describing, fields are matched by name and compatible type, and as a type evolves by adding fields, out-of-date receivers still function on the part of the type they recognize
